semantic_correction.stem: An asymptomatic young adult male asks whether a formal monthly testicular self-exam is recommended as a routine cancer-screening test. Which response is most accurate?

options.A: There is no standard routine screening test; new lumps, swelling, or a change in how a testicle feels should be evaluated promptly.
options.B: Monthly self-exam is proven to reduce testicular-cancer mortality and is recommended as routine screening for asymptomatic adult men.
options.C: A painless testicular lump can usually be observed without evaluation because cancer-related lumps are generally painful.
options.D: Routine ultrasound is the preferred population screening test for asymptomatic young men even when examination and history are normal.

semantic_correction.rationale: The National Cancer Institute's Testicular Cancer Screening page, updated May 8, 2025 and current in 2026, states that there is no standard or routine screening test for early detection of testicular cancer. NCI also states that no studies have shown that self-exams, clinician exams, or other screening tests in asymptomatic men reduce the risk of dying from testicular cancer. In contrast, NCI's symptom guidance advises medical evaluation for a painless lump or swelling, a change in how a testicle feels, sudden scrotal fluid accumulation, or testicular/scrotal discomfort. Therefore routine self-examination should not be presented as an evidence-proven screening mandate, but new changes warrant prompt evaluation.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Distinguish the absence of a standard routine testicular-cancer screening test in asymptomatic men from the need to evaluate new testicular symptoms or changes promptly.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — screening/symptom education
audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item accurately separates population screening from symptom recognition without claiming mortality benefit from routine self-exam.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches NCI's screening statement and symptom-evaluation guidance.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. NCI states that mortality benefit from routine self-exam in asymptomatic men has not been established.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. A painless lump or swelling is a recognized possible presentation and warrants evaluation.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. NCI does not recommend routine ultrasound as a standard population screening test in asymptomatic men.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone accurately combines the screening evidence and symptom-response guidance.
cueing_check: All four options are testicular-cancer screening or evaluation statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
